chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Durust, from Muhammad ibn Al-Fadl Al-Hashimi, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) along with my brothers, so we said, 'We intend the Hajj, and some of us are Sarurah (those who have not performed Hajj before).' He said: 'Upon you is the Tamattu', for we do not fear a Sultan (ruling authority) regarding the Tamattu with the Umrah to the Hajj, and keeping away from the intoxicants, and the wiping upon the two socks.'

key_terms.التَّمَتُّعِ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately with a break in between)
key_terms.الْخُفَّيْنِ: Al-Khuffayn (the two socks, worn over feet for wiping during wudu)
key_terms.صَرُورَةٌ: Sarurah (one who has not performed Hajj before, or a novice in Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred type of Hajj according to Imam al-Sadiq and what are its associated ritual benefits?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) recommends Hajj al-Tamattu' as the preferred form of pilgrimage, citing its ease and the lack of political restriction ('sultan') against it. He specifically links this preference to the permissibility of wiping over socks (*khuffayn*) during ablution and avoiding intoxicants, reflecting key jurisprudential distinctions in Shia fiqh. This narration underscores the practical flexibility granted to pilgrims, emphasizing ritual convenience alongside spiritual devotion.
